headline: Extended Hebert Development's deal for 55 Old Lisbon Road; gave first passage to curbside trash ordinance and final passage to amusement permit rules.
summary: Residents spoke during public comment on elections, trash cans, and housing. The meeting also sold 35 Beechwood Avenue for $1,500 and accepted $18,168 in forfeiture funds. The hearing on mobile home lot rent increases was continued to the next meeting.
decisions: Approved an extension of the Purchase and Sale Agreement with Hebert Development for 55 Old Lisbon Road, 7-0.
Continued the public hearing and first passage of the mobile home lot rent ordinance to the next regular meeting, 7-0.
Approved first passage of amendments to the solid waste ordinance allowing curbside collection for certain owner-occupied mixed-use properties, 7-0, and continued the public hearing.
Approved final passage of amendments to the amusement and entertainment ordinance on special amusement permits, 7-0.
Approved accepting Maine Bureau of Highway Safety grant funds for Lewiston police traffic enforcement, 7-0.
Approved a quitclaim deed releasing the city's interest in 304 East Avenue to the owner, 7-0.
Approved transfer of up to $18,168 in forfeiture funds to the City of Lewiston Drug Enforcement Program account, 7-0.
Approved the sale of 35 Beechwood Avenue to Brandon Lopez for $1,500, 7-0.
Confirmed Jeffrey Padham to the Housing Committee, 7-0.
Appointed Benjamin Thorne to the Lewiston-Auburn Community Forestry Board, 7-0.
Appointed Jonathan Hussey to the Lewiston Housing Authority Board of Commissioners, 7-0.
Approved the October 6, 2026 meeting minutes as prepared by the City Clerk, 6-0, with Councilor Roy abstaining.

CITY OF LEWISTON 
 
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 20, 2026 
 
REGULAR MEETING HELD IN THE COUNCIL ROOM AT 6:30 P.M. 
 
THE HONORABLE CARL L. SHELINE, MAYOR, PRESIDING. 
          
PRESENT: Mayor Sheline, Councilors Nagine, Longchamps, Harriman, Roy, Noble, Chittim, 
and Martel, City Administrator Bryan Kaenrath, Deputy City Administrator Brian O’Malley, and 
City Clerk Kathleen Montejo.  
 
EXECUTIVE SESSION 
 
VOTE (355-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To enter into an Executive Session, pursuant to MRSA Title 1, section 405(6) (c), to discuss the 
acquisition or disposition of Real Estate, of which the premature disclosure of the information 
would prejudice the competitive bargaining position of the City.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
Executive Session began at 6:31pm and ended at 7:00 pm. 
 
Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag. 
 
VOTE (356-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
  
To dispense with the reading of the minutes of the meeting of October 6, 2026, and to accept and 
place them on file as prepared by the City Clerk.  Passed - Vote 6-0 (Councilor Roy abstained, 
noting he was not present at the October 6 Council meeting.) 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
Janet Beaudoin, Ward 2 – Reported she was at the polls last week greeting voters and a voter’s 
aide came up to her and asked what political party she was in. She said she was not permitted to 
answer that question while in the voting area and the aide said if she was in a certain party, he 
would tell the voter he was assisting to vote for her. She expressed concerns about election 
engineering when the Clerk is not present.  
 
Ronnie Paradis, Ward 4 – Senior citizens are having a hard time getting the new trash cans out to 
the curb due to their size. Lewiston reacts to issues but does not show any pro-active activity.  
The city is not ready for winter. Seniors do not have any money for heating oil. Need warming 
centers in addition to homeless shelters. At the next Council meeting, the Council needs to be 
ready to take action on this issue. 
 
Lisa Jones, Ward 2 – Residents are watching an election be violated in real time, this is a sham 
election. The federal government is pressing charges for non-citizens voting. In the Sun Journal 
interview, Councilor Harriman said an email about accusations of inappropriate actions were
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 20, 2026 
                             
2 
 
sent to the Maine Wire but the email was actually sent to city leadership first, and that email was 
ignored. 
 
Debra Hibred Bredo, Ward 6 – No faith in elected officials. Silence speaks volumes. You are 
dismissing a victim’s experience, allowing students to see a person in authority acting this way, 
Council needs to open an investigation. 
 
Matt Agren, Ward 4 – Lewiston has a violence problem. Hold the Mayor to a higher standard. 
We are not honoring Domestic Violence Awareness Month. 
 
Andrew Jones, Ward 2 – There was too much politics at the last Council meeting. This body says 
it is non-partisan but clearly is not. Some people feel the victim isn’t credible. What if it was a 
member of your family allegedly violated? Would you want to check into it or let it slide? 
 
Laurie Horton, Ward 2 – The “Me Too” movement started twenty years ago with Bill Cobsy, P 
Diddy, others. We have our own version here with Clr. Harriman. Where is the transparency? 
 
Bob McDonald, Ward 6 – Voters are being helped casting their votes, they should already know 
how to vote. People are building low income apartments and receive TIFs, the TIF money should 
be given back to the taxpayers who support the projects. The city’s welfare numbers are very 
high. Lisbon Street has no businesses, only non-profits.  
 
Jay Rodrigue, Ward 6 – In Lewiston, everything is non-taxable. People not paying property taxes 
should start paying them. There is already damage in Gavreau Apartments, a fairly new property. 
Lisbon Street needs to be cleaned up. 
 
CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT 
 
City Administration is hosting information sessions for Business Opportunity Grants to help new 
and existing Lewiston businesses. Phase Two of the Community Engagement and Accountability 
(CEA) program is underway and the City Administrator and Chief of Police met with Lewiston 
business leaders and non-profit leaders to develop legislative proposals to address youth gun 
violence issues. The Rec Department has two free family Halloween events coming up featuring 
pumpkin carving, arts and crafts, games, face painting and more. Please visit the Rec Department 
website for more details.  A Veterans Day ceremony will be held at Veterans Memorial Park at 
10am featuring the Patriot Freedom Riders. The city is seeking interested residents to volunteer 
to serve on our city boards and committees.  Early voting is available through October 29. A 
remembrance ceremony will be held on Oct 25 to recognize the third anniversary of the mass 
shooting incident.  Atlas Structural Systems will be holding a grand opening on October 21.  
 
ORDER, AUTHORIZING THE ACCEPTANCE OF FUNDS FROM THE MAINE 
BUREAU OF HIGHWAY SAFETY 
 
VOTE (357-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To approve the Order, Authorizing the Acceptance of Funds from the Maine Bureau of Highway
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 20, 2026 
                             
3 
 
Safety: 
 
Whereas, the Lewiston Police Department was awarded funding from the Maine Bureau of  
Highway Safety   
 
Whereas, this funding is to be utilized for overtime patrols for enforcement of distracted driving,  
pedestrian safety, speed, seatbelt usage and impaired driving laws  
 
Whereas, this funding is to be utilized for Forensic Phlebotomist and Drug Recognition Expert  
call out overtime costs 
 
Whereas, the grant period is 10/1/2026 – 09/15/2027 
 
Whereas, this grant supports the continued efforts of the Lewiston Police Department to enforce  
traffic safety laws 
 
Now, Therefore, Be It Ordered by the City Council of the City of Lewiston t o approve the 
acceptance of grant funds from the Maine Bureau of Highway Safety. 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, AUTHORIZING EXECUTION OF MUNICIPAL QUITCLAIM DEED FOR 
REAL ESTATE LOCATED AT 304 EAST AVENUE 
 
VOTE (358-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To approve the Order, Authorizing Execution of Municipal Quitclaim Deed for Real Estate located 
at 304 East Avenue: 
 
Whereas, the former owner, Stephen J McCarron, failed to pay his bills on a timely basis for 304  
East Avenue (Tax Map 173, Lot 52, Parcel 00-006876); and 
 
Whereas, a tax lien was filed on June 16, 2010 (Book 7952 Page 308) and matured on December  
16, 2011, in the amount of $2,064.55; and 
 
Whereas, a tax lien was filed on June 17, 2011 (Book 8181 Page 135) and matured on December  
17, 2012, in the amount of $2,085.63; and 
 
Whereas, a tax lien was filed on June 13, 2012 (Book 8417 Page 286) and matured on December  
13, 2013, in the amount of $2,115.72; and 
 
Whereas, a tax lien was filed on June 19, 2013 (Book 8700 Page 12) and matured on December  
19, 2014, in the amount of $2,118.33, and 
 
Whereas, a tax lien was filed on June 18, 2014 (Book 8934 Page 276) and matured on December  
18, 2015, in the amount of $2,182.55; and
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 20, 2026 
                             
4 
 
 
Whereas, a tax lien was filed on June 14, 2017 (Book 9616 Page 134) and matured on December 14,  
2018, in the amount of $1,877.39; and 
 
Whereas, a tax lien was filed on June 21, 2018 (Book 9865 Page 256) and matured on December  
21, 2019, in the amount of $1,794.70, and 
 
Whereas, a tax lien was filed on June 18, 2019 (Book 10107 Page 209) and matured on December  
19, 2020, in the amount of $1,848.42; and 
 
Whereas, a tax lien was filed on June 15, 2021 (Book 10773 Page 61) and matured on December 15,  
2022, in the amount of $1,746.59; and 
 
Whereas, payment has been received. 
 
Now, Therefore, Be It Ordered by the City Council of the City of Lewiston, that a quitclaim deed 
is hereby authorized to release the City’s interest in the property located at 304 East Avenue to the 
owner.  
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
AUTHORIZATION TO ACCEPT TRANSFER OF FORFEITURE FUNDS 
 
VOTE (359-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
That pursuant to Title 15, Maine Revised Statutes Annotated, Section 5824(3) and Section 
5822(4)(A), the City Council hereby acknowledges and approves the transfer of $18,168 or any 
portion thereof, in the case of the State of Maine vs. Abdirahman S. Moham ud, Docket Number 
ANDCD-CR-2019-03094 Court Records, being funds forfeited pursuant to the court process. It is 
further acknowledged that these funds shall be credited to the ‘City of Lewiston Drug Enforcement 
Program’ account.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, APPROVING THE DISPOSITION OF 35 BEECHWOOD AVENUE 
 
VOTE (360-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
  
To adopt the Order, Approving the Disposition of 35 Beechwood Avenue: 
 
Whereas, the City Council voted to sell the tax acquired parcel located at 35 Beechwood Avenue  
at their 2/25/2020 meeting and 
 
Whereas, the City received an offer for the parcel through the City’s Realtor DuBois Realty; and 
 
Whereas, Brandon Lopez offered $1,500 for 35 Beechwood Avenue
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 20, 2026 
                             
5 
 
Now, Therefore, Be It Ordered by the City Council of the City of Lewiston, t o approve the 
disposition of 35 Beechwood Avenue and authorize the City Administrator to execute all necessary 
legal documents. 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FIRST PASSAGE REGARDING AN AMENDMENT TO THE 
RESIDENTIAL RENTAL PROPERTY ORDINANCE TO REGULATE LOT RENT 
INCREASES IN MOBILE HOME PARKS 
 
City Attorney Mike Carey and Housing Committee members Craig Saddlemire and Katie Lauze 
made a presentation to Council regarding the details of the draft ordinance.  
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comments.   
John Horton – Thank you to everyone who is working on this issue. Please look at state law. 
Matt Agren, Ward 4 – This presentation should have been held in a workshop session, not in the 
middle of the meeting. It is a slippery slope to punish outside investors for owning lots of mobile 
homes around the country. 
Kathy Wayne, Ward 6 – As a senior citizen in a mobile home park, she is paying high lot rents. 
Many seniors are working to be able to afford rents, they are paying taxes too. 
The Mayor then closed the hearing. 
 
VOTE (361-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Nagine, seconded by Councilor Chittim: 
 
To continue the public hearing and First Passage to the next regular meeting.  
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
At this time, the Council took a ten-minute recess. 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FIRST PASSAGE REGARDING AN AMENDMENT TO THE 
SOLID WASTE ORDINANCE TO AUTHORIZE CURBSIDE COLLECTION FOR 
CERTAIN OWNER-OCCUPIED MIXED-USE PROPERTIES 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comments. No residents 
spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing.  
 
VOTE (362-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim , seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
That the proposed amendments to the City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 62 “Solid Waste”, Article 
I “In General”, Sec. 62-11 “Definitions” and Sec. 62-13 “Municipal collection of solid waste and 
recyclable materials”, receive first passage by a roll call vote  and that the public hearing on said 
ordinance be continued to the next regularly scheduled City Council meeting. 
Passed - Vote 7-0
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 20, 2026 
                             
6 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FINAL PASSAGE REGARDING AN AMENDMENT TO THE 
AMUSEMENTS AND ENTERTAINMENT ORDINANCE REGARDING APPROVALS 
FOR NEW SPECIAL AMUSEMENT PERMITS 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comments. No residents 
spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing.  
 
VOTE (363-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
That the proposed amendments to the City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 10 “Amusements and 
Entertainments”, Article III “Special Amusement Permits”, Division 2 “Permit”, receive final 
passage by a roll call vote.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, AUTHORIZING THE CITY ADMINISTRATOR TO EXECUTE AN 
EXTENSION OF THE PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT WITH HEBERT 
DEVELOPMENT FOR 55 OLD LISBON ROAD 
 
VOTE (364-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Chittim: 
 
To approve the Order, Authorizing the City Administrator to Execute an Extension of the Purchase 
and Sale Agreement with Hebert Development for 55 Old Lisbon Road: 
 
Whereas, the City of Lewiston tax acquired 55 Old Lisbon Road through matured liens dated  
3/18/2021; and 
 
Whereas, the City received an offer for the parcel through the City’s Realtor DuBois Realty from  
Hebert Development for $750,000; and 
 
Whereas, at its meeting on July 15, 2025, the City Council authorized the City Administrator to  
execute a Purchase and Sale Agreement for the property that included a 120-day due diligence  
period; and 
 
Whereas, Hebert Development requested a 12 month extension of the Purchase and Sale  
Agreement to complete additional due diligence 
 
Whereas, at its meeting on December, 2 2025, the City Council authorized the City  
Administrator to extend the Purchase and Sale Agreement for 12 months, retroactive to  
November 14, 2025 
 
Whereas, Hebert Development and the City of Lewiston Economic & Community Development  
staff have worked diligently and in good faith, and the project partners are optimistic a  
neighborhood housing development with significant community benefits can be achieved with an  
additional 6 month extension; and 
 
Whereas, the developer and the city staff will use the additional time provided by an extension to
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 20, 2026 
                             
7 
 
work on due diligence and negotiations on more than one large development project; and 
 
Whereas, Credit enhancement/tax increment financing for up to 75% pending a verified pro  
forma and additional public hearing and City Council approval; and 
 
Now, Therefore, Be It Ordered by the City Council of the City of  Lewiston, t o approve an 
extension of the Purchase and Sale Agreement with Hebert Development for 55 Old Lisbon 
Road and authorize the City Administrator to execute all necessary legal documents. 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
APPOINTMENT TO THE HOUSING COMMITTEE 
 
VOTE (365-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To confirm the Mayor’s appointment of the following resident as a member of the Housing 
Committee for the position of Owner of Multi-Unit Property:   
 
Jeffrey Padham, 49 Bardwell Street – term to expire Jan 4, 2028 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
APPOINTMENT TO THE LEWISTON-AUBURN COMMUNITY FORESTRY BOARD 
 
VOTE (366-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To appoint the following resident as a member of the Lewiston -Auburn Community Forestry 
Board:   
 
Benjamin Thorne, 285 Scribner Boulevard – term to expire Jan 4, 2027 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
APPOINTMENT TO THE LEWISTON HOUSING AUTHORITY BOARD OF 
COMMISSIONERS 
 
VOTE (367-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To confirm the Mayor’s nomination and to appoint the following resident as a member of the 
Board of Commissioners of the Lewiston Housing Authority:   
 
Jonathan Hussey, 571 Pond Road, term to expire Sept. 17, 2031 – citizen representative 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0
CITY COUNCIL  OCTOBER 20, 2026 
                             
8 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
No members of the public offered comments at this time. 
 
REPORTS AND UPDATES 
 
Councilor Harriman reported the School Committee, at their meeting last night, approved filed 
trips, received department updates and approved various policies.  
 
OTHER BUSINESS 
 
Councilor Nagine noted he asked the Public Health Committee to look into the ban on the sale of 
Kratom in the city.  
 
VOTE (368-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Longchamps: 
 
To adjourn at 10:10 P.M.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
A true record, Attest: 
 
 
 
Kathleen M. Montejo, MMC  
City Clerk 
Lewiston, Maine
